title: Scheduler-kernel affinity inversion causing P99 token latency spike
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-09 we observed a sustained P99 token latency increase (~2.5x) across a subset of hosted inference pods serving LlamaX-13B-like models. The spike correlated with a scheduler refactor merged the same day. Root cause analysis shows an "affinity inversion" where the scheduler's new scoring heuristic preferred a low-latency kernel variant for short sequences but erroneously routed many long-context requests to that variant due to a TTL/sequence-length bucketing bug. The chosen kernel had suboptimal attention tiling for long sequences and triggered repeated KV cache evictions under concurrent requests, amplifying tail latency.

Timeline:
- 2026-02-09 09:12 UTC: First alert triggered by SLO monitor (P99 token latency > 500ms on runtime-prod-eu-*)
- 2026-02-09 09:18 UTC: On-call (Marco Ruiz) paged; incident declared.
- 2026-02-09 09:30 UTC: Rollback of scheduler refactor (merge r/feat/scheduler-affinity v2) performed; immediate partial improvement observed.
- 2026-02-09 10:15 UTC: Full mitigation: force-routing of long-context traffic to stable kernel variant (runtime-safety policy) rolled out.
- 2026-02-09 11:00 UTC: SLOs returned near-normal; incident moved to Post-Incident Review (PIR).

Detection and signals:
- Primary signal: SLO alert for token P99 latency spike. Secondary signals: increase in CPU utilization on specific GPU hosts, repeated KV cache flush events in logs, and higher retry rates from the request router.
- Relevant dashboards: /dashboards/runtime/latency-token-p99, /dashboards/runtime/kernel-selection-breakdown. Incident runbook page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-02-09-scheduler-affinity
- GitHub: rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4890

Root cause (summary): The scheduler refactor introduced a non-idempotent bucketing change: a TTL cache used to memoize kernel affinity keyed on request class was missing the sequence-length ceiling when re-hydrating entries. On warm paths, long-context requests were matched to the short-seq optimized kernel. That kernel's attention tiling and KV layout are inefficient for longer sequences; combined with continuous-batching heuristics it led to repeated cache churn and head-of-line blocking for concurrent requests.

Why this slipped through:
- Orig refactor had unit tests for short/long routing but did not exercise concurrent KV cache eviction scenarios.
- Canary deployment covered low traffic and short sequences; QA harness lacked a long-context, concurrency-heavy workload.

Immediate mitigations already taken:
1) Rolled back refactor (PR link above) to restore previous scheduler behavior.
2) Emergency routing policy: mark long-context classes as "pinned-stable-kernel" for 72 hours.
3) Increased observability: enabled kernel-selection trace sampling at 100% for one hour and captured KV eviction metrics.

Follow-up action items (owners and due dates):
- A1: Fix TTL bucketing logic to include sequence-length ceiling on cache key rehydration; add unit + concurrency tests. Owner: Chen Li. Due: 2026-02-24. Tracking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4922
- A2: Add synthetic e2e test workload for long-context concurrent traffic to CI/perf-harness (simulate 1k concurrent streams at 1.5k tokens). Owner: Marco Ruiz. Due: 2026-02-28. Test plan doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/long-context-harness
- A3: Expand canary matrix to include long-seq traffic and KV-cache-stress scenarios; update deployment checklist. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-01.
- A4: Implement a scheduler invariant gate that rejects affinity scoring updates failing a regression threshold on locally simulated KV churn. Owner: Diego Fernandez. Due: 2026-03-08.
- A5: Perform kernel profiling to measure attention tiling inefficiencies and derive a micro-optimization plan; coordinate with Applied ML. Owner: Elena Korolev. Due: 2026-03-05.
- A6: Postmortem write-up and customer communications (template) for impacted enterprise tenants. Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2026-02-22.

Verification and rollout plan:
- Patch PRs will land behind feature flags. Run the long-context harness in CI; require no regression in P99 token latency and no >5% increase in KV eviction rate for 48h on staging before canary.
- Canary rollout plan: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with rollback triggers defined (token P99 exceed baseline +15% or KV eviction increase >25%).

Monitoring to add (metrics & dashboards):
- kernel_selection.route_mismatch_ratio (new)
- kv_cache.evictions_per_min by model/tenant
- scheduler.affinity_score_distribution (histogram)
- per-pod token P99 stratified by sequence-length buckets (0-128,129-512,513-2048,>2048)

Communication notes:
- Engineering exec summary sent to GTM and Sales at 2026-02-10 14:00 UTC. Draft for customer incident letters ready for review.
- Support playbook: instruct support to apply the temporary routing override for any reported long-context latency tickets until fixes are live.

Retrospective lessons:
- Expand perf canary dimensions (sequence-length + concurrency orthogonalization).
- Make kernel-selection logic explicitly guarded by a sequence-length compatibility matrix; treat heuristic changes as high-risk.
- Improve the perf harness to include KV-cache eviction scenarios as a first-class failure mode.

Relevant artifacts and links:
- Incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-02-09-scheduler-affinity
- Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4890
- Fix PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4922
- Long-context harness doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/long-context-harness
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime-token-p99

Open questions for follow-up meeting:
- Should we add explicit kernel capability metadata (max_sequence_length_recommendation) to the model catalog and expose it in routing decisions? (vote: leaning yes)
- What SLO guardrails should block scheduler heuristic changes from auto-deploying? Who signs off? (proposed: runtime-owners + perf lead)
